title: Katherine Johnson double-checked a spaceflight
beats: Before his orbital flight, John Glenn asked for one more check.

NASA had used electronic computers to calculate the course for Friendship Seven. Glenn asked mathematician Katherine Johnson to check those results. She ran the equations by hand and found that the computer's numbers were right.

archive.credit: NASA Langley Research Center, portrait of Katherine Johnson, 1971. Used in factual editorial context under NASA’s media guidelines.
archive.label: KATHERINE JOHNSON · NASA PORTRAIT, 1971

title: The Wright brothers’ twelve-second flight
beats: The Wright brothers' first flight lasted twelve seconds.
Orville flew just one hundred twenty feet. That short distance marked a breakthrough for controlled, powered flight.

archive.credit: John T. Daniels, first flight at Kitty Hawk, 1903. Library of Congress, Wright Brothers Negatives. No known publication restrictions.
archive.label: FIRST FLIGHT · LIBRARY OF CONGRESS

title: How Henrietta Leavitt turned stars into distance markers
beats: Henrietta Leavitt found a pattern in pulsing stars.
Brighter Cepheid stars pulse more slowly. Her discovery gave astronomers a way to estimate distances across space.

archive.credit: William Henry, portrait published in The Woman Citizen, 1921. Public domain in the United States, via Wikimedia Commons.
archive.label: HENRIETTA LEAVITT · PORTRAIT, 1921

title: What C. V. Raman discovered about scattered light
labels: MOLECULES SHIFT SOME OF THE LIGHT
beats: Shine one color of light at a molecule.
Raman found that a little of the scattered light changes color. The shift tells us something about the molecule.

archive.credit: C. V. Raman, The Modern Review, 1914, via Wikimedia Commons. Public-domain historical publication.
archive.label: C. V. RAMAN · THE MODERN REVIEW, 1914

title: चंद्रशेखर ने तारों की कौन-सी सीमा खोजी?
labels: सूरज के द्रव्यमान का लगभग 1.4 गुना
beats: एक सफ़ेद बौना तारा कितना भारी हो सकता है?
सुब्रह्मण्यन चंद्रशेखर ने इसकी सीमा निकाली। यह सूरज के द्रव्यमान का लगभग एक दशमलव चार गुना है।

title: Corals are animals
beats: Is coral a plant or an animal?
Corals are animals. A stony coral colony is made of tiny polyps that build hard skeletons beneath them.

title: Venus spins slower than it orbits
beats: Venus can finish a year before it finishes one spin.
One trip around the Sun takes two hundred twenty-five Earth days. That spin takes two hundred forty-three.

title: Why the Moon turns red
beats: Why does the Moon turn red?
During a lunar eclipse, Earth's atmosphere filters sunlight and bends reddish light toward the Moon.

title: An octopus has three hearts
beats: Why does an octopus have three hearts?
Two pump blood to the gills to pick up oxygen. The third pumps it to the rest of the body.

title: How one raindrop splits sunlight
beats: A whole rainbow starts with one tiny drop.
Watch what happens to the sunlight. It bends on the way in, bounces once inside, and comes out as a fan of colors.

title: Why a clear sky looks blue
beats: Is the sky blue because it reflects the ocean?
No. Air molecules scatter blue light more than red. That sends blue light toward you from across the sky.

title: A second rainbow flips the colors
beats: Why does a double rainbow reverse colors?
Light in the outer bow reflects twice inside raindrops, which reverses the order of the colors.

title: The Moon is slowly drifting away
beats: Astronauts left mirrors on the Moon.
We still bounce lasers off them to measure the distance. Turns out the Moon is drifting away about as fast as your fingernails grow.
writing_facts: Apollo astronauts left laser reflectors on the Moon.
Scientists measure the time it takes light to make the round trip.
The Moon recedes about 3.8 centimeters (1.5 inches) every year, roughly as fast as fingernails grow.

title: What are Saturn’s rings made of?
beats: What are Saturn's rings made of?
They're billions of pieces of ice and rock, moving around Saturn at different speeds.

title: Mercury goes around the Sun twice in a day
labels: 176 EARTH DAYS FROM SUNRISE TO SUNRISE
beats: How long is a day on Mercury?
From sunrise to sunrise takes about one hundred seventy-six Earth days, twice as long as Mercury's orbit.

title: Jupiter has the shortest day
labels: A SPIN TAKES ABOUT TEN HOURS
beats: Which planet has the shortest day?
Jupiter spins once in about ten hours. In Cassini’s time-lapse, you can see neighboring cloud bands move at different speeds.

title: Uranus spins on its side
labels: ONE POLE FACES THE SUN FOR DECADES
beats: Which planet spins on its side?
Uranus. Its axis is tilted about ninety-eight degrees, so each pole can face the Sun for decades.

title: Sunsets on Mars can glow blue
beats: Why can sunsets on Mars glow blue?
Fine dust in the Martian atmosphere makes the blue light near the setting Sun stand out.
